15465-parisian-points-of-view.description: A book by Ludovic Halévy. There is even a legend--although how solid a foundation it may have in fact I do not dare to discuss--there is a legend that the lady-superior of a certain convent near Paris was so fascinated by _The Abbé Constantin_, and so thoroughly convinced of the piety of its author, that she ordered all his other works, receiving in due season the lively volumes wherein are recorded the sayings and doings of Monsieur and Madame Cardinal, and of the two lovely daughters of Monsieur and Madame

arxiv-2102-03315.title: Think you have Solved Direct-Answer Question Answering? Try ARC-DA, the Direct-Answer AI2 Reasoning Challenge
arxiv-2102-03315.creator: Sumithra Bhakthavatsalam, Daniel Khashabi, Tushar Khot, Bhavana Dalvi Mishra
arxiv-2102-03315.description: Abstract We present the ARC-DA dataset, a direct-answer (‘‘open response’’, ‘‘freeform’’) version of the ARC (AI2 Reasoning Challenge) multiple-choice dataset. While ARC has been influential in the community, its multiple-choice format is unrepresentative of real-world questions, and multiple choice formats can be particularly susceptible to artifacts.

arxiv-2105-12897.title: Computable topological abelian groups
arxiv-2105-12897.creator: Martino Lupini, Alexander Melnikov, and Andre Nies
arxiv-2105-12897.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Martino Lupini, Alexander Melnikov, and Andre Nies. We study the algorithmic content of Pontryagin - van Kampen duality. We prove that the dualization is computable in the important cases of compact and locally compact totally disconnected Polish abelian groups. The applications of our main results include solutions to questions of Kihara and Ng about presentations of connected Polish spaces, and an unexpected arithmetical characterisation of direct products of solenoid groups among all Polish groups.

arxiv-2210-00521.title: Leveraging unsupervised data and domain adaptation for deep regression in low-cost sensor calibration
arxiv-2210-00521.creator: Swapnil Dey, Vipul Arora, Sachchida Nand Tripathi
arxiv-2210-00521.description: Abstract Air quality monitoring is becoming an essential task with rising awareness about air quality. Low cost air quality sensors are easy to deploy but are not as reliable as the costly and bulky reference monitors. The low quality sensors can be calibrated against the reference monitors with the help of deep learning.

arxiv-2211-01655.description: Abstract A novel technique for broadband high-precision mass measurements of short-lived exotic nuclides is reported. It is based on the isochronous mass spectrometry (IMS) and realizes simultaneous determinations of revolution time and velocity of short-lived stored ions at the cooler storage ring CSRe in Lanzhou.

arxiv-2308-00787.title: Evaluating Spiking Neural Network On Neuromorphic Platform For Human Activity Recognition Conference: Proceedings of the 2023 International Symposium on Wearable Computers; October 8–12, 2023; Cancun, Quintana Roo, Mexico Proceedings of the 2023 International Symposium on Wearable Computers (ISWC ’2
arxiv-2308-00787.creator: Sizhen Bian, Michele Magno
arxiv-2308-00787.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Sizhen Bian, Michele Magno. Energy efficiency and low latency are crucial requirements for designing wearable AI-empowered human activity recognition systems, due to the hard constraints of battery operations and closed-loop feedback. While neural network models have been extensively compressed to match the stringent edge requirements, spiking neural networks and event-based sensing are recently emerging as promising solutions to further improve performance due to their inherent energy efficiency and capacity to process spatiotemporal data in very low latency.

arxiv-2402-13315.title: Gas Metallicity of Ram-Pressure Stripped Galaxies at Intermediate Redshift with MUSE Data
arxiv-2402-13315.creator: A. Khoram, B. Poggianti, A. Moretti, B. Vulcani, M. Radovich, A. Werle, M. Gullieuszik, J. Richard
arxiv-2402-13315.description: Abstract Extraplanar tails of ionized stripped gas, extending up to several tens of kiloparsecs beyond the stellar disk, are often observed in ram-pressure stripped (RPS) galaxies in low redshift clusters. Recent studies have identified similar tails also at high redshift and we here present the first analysis of the chemical composition of such tails beyond the local universe.

arxiv-2407-02697.title: Design and Development of PainBit: a Portable Device for Supporting Patients with Chronic Pain to Log their Pain
arxiv-2407-02697.creator: Arsh Saleem Department of Systems and Computer Engineering Carleton University, Beck Langstone Department of Human-Computer Interaction Carleton University, Alicia Ouskine Department of Human-Computer Interaction Carleton University, Fateme Rajabiyazdi Department of Systems and Computer Engineering
arxiv-2407-02697.description: Abstract Recently, we have seen growing interest among patients with chronic conditions to track their health-related data. There are many wearable devices available to track different health data. However, tracking pain is mostly done by using pen and paper or mobile apps. In collaboration with a healthcare professional we designed a portable pain tracker, PainBit.

arxiv-2408-10042.title: Entire hypersurfaces of constant scalar curvature in Minkowski space
arxiv-2408-10042.creator: Pierre Bayard, Andrea Seppi
arxiv-2408-10042.description: Abstract . We show that every regular domain 𝒟 \mathcal{D} in Minkowski space ℝ n , 1 \mathbb{R}^{n,1} which is not a wedge admits an entire hypersurface whose domain of dependence is 𝒟 \mathcal{D} and whose scalar curvature is a prescribed constant (or function, under suitable hypotheses) in ( − ∞ , 0 ) (-\infty,0) .

arxiv-2502-06455.title: Analysis of a finite element method for the Stokes–Poisson–Boltzmann equations
arxiv-2502-06455.creator: Abeer F. AlSohaim, Ricardo Ruiz-Baier, Segundo Villa-Fuentes
arxiv-2502-06455.description: Abstract We define a finite element method for the coupling of Stokes and nonlinear Poisson–Boltzmann equations. The novelty in the formulation is that the coupling from the electric potential to the drag in the momentum balance is rewritten as a weighted advection term.

arxiv-2503-21444.title: Automated Analysis of Pricings in SaaS-based Information Systems
arxiv-2503-21444.creator: Alejandro García-Fernández, José Antonio Parejo, Pablo Trinidad, Antonio Ruiz-Cortés
arxiv-2503-21444.description: Abstract Software as a Service (SaaS) pricing models, encompassing features, usage limits, plans, and add-ons, have grown exponentially in complexity, evolving from offering tens to thousands of configuration options. This rapid expansion poses significant challenges for the development and operation of SaaS-based Information Systems (IS), as manual management of such configurations becomes time-consuming, error-prone, and ultimately unsustainable.

arxiv-2509-10015.title: A Framework for AI-Supported Mediation in Community-based Online Collaboration
arxiv-2509-10015.creator: SOOBIN CHO
arxiv-2509-10015.description: Abstract Reference Format: Soobin Cho, Mark Zachry, and David W. McDonald. 2025. A Framework for AI-Supported Mediation in Community-based Online Collaboration. arXiv:2509.10015 [cs.HC] https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.10015 1 Introduction: From Moderation to Mediation in Online Collaboration Online spaces involve diverse communities engaging in various forms of collaboration, which naturally give rise to discussions, some of which inevitably escalate into conflict or disputes.

arxiv-2510-18798.title: WebSeer: Training Deeper Search Agents through Reinforcement Learning with Self-Reflection
arxiv-2510-18798.creator: Guanzhong He, Zhen Yang, Jinxin Liu, Bin Xu, Lei Hou, Juanzi Li
arxiv-2510-18798.description: Abstract Search agents have achieved significant advancements in enabling intelligent information retrieval and decision-making within interactive environments. Although reinforcement learning has been employed to train agentic models capable of more dynamic interactive retrieval, existing methods are limited by shallow tool-use depth and the accumulation of errors over multiple iterative interactions.

arxiv-2602-05996.title: Orthogonal Self-Attention
arxiv-2602-05996.creator: Leo Zhang, James Martens
arxiv-2602-05996.description: Abstract Softmax Self-Attention (SSA) is a key component of Transformer architectures. However, when utilised within skipless architectures, which aim to improve representation learning, recent work has highlighted the inherent instability of SSA due to inducing rank collapse and poorly-conditioned Jacobians.

pmc-11340234.title: Perinatal intimate partner violence among teen mothers and children’s attachment disorders in Rwanda: potential mediating factors
pmc-11340234.creator: Martin Nshimyumukiza, Japhet Niyonsenga, Clementine Kanazayire, Simeon Gitimbwa Sebatukura, Jean Mutabaruka
pmc-11340234.description: Background: The alarming prevalence of teen mothers’ exposure to perinatal intimate partner violence (IPV, 8.3-67%) and attachment disorders (ADs) among their children is a global concern, especially in sub-Saharan Africa with high teenage pregnancy rates. This study, therefore, aimed to examine the link between teen IPV and AD in their offspring.

pmc-11406725.title: Prospective acceptability of mass drug administration for malaria in Kedougou region in Senegal: a mixed method study
pmc-11406725.creator: Eva Legendre, Antoine Ndiaye, Ndèye Mareme Sougou, Jean Gaudart, El Hadj Ba, Valéry Ridde, Jordi Landier
pmc-11406725.description: BackgroundIn Senegalese high-burden regions, the existing package of interventions is insufficient to reach the malaria elimination goal. Asymptomatic carriers of Plasmodium contribute significantly to malaria persistence and are not targeted by current interventions. The systematic treatment of all individuals in a community (mass drug administration, MDA) is a relevant intervention to tackle asymptomatic infections.

pmc-11450591.title: The thickness of the retinal nerve fiber layer, macula, and ganglion cell‐inner plexiform layer in people with drug‐resistant epilepsy
pmc-11450591.creator: Yujie Chen, Weixi Xiong, Lu Lu, Xintong Wu, Le Cao, Jiani Chen, Yingfeng Xiao, Josemir W Sander, Bo Wu, Dong Zhou
pmc-11450591.description: ObjectiveUsing Optical coherence tomography (OCT), we evaluated the association between peripapillary retinal nerve fiber, macular thickness, macular ganglion cell‐inner plexiform layer, and drug resistance.MethodsIn this cross‐sectional study, we recruited people diagnosed with epilepsy and healthy controls. People with epilepsy were further stratified as drug‐resistant or non‐drug‐resistant based on their response to anti‐seizure medications.

pmc-11461058.title: A computational approach to selective attention in embodied approaches to cognitive archaeology
pmc-11461058.creator: Axel Constant, Laura Desirèe Di Paolo, Avel Guénin-Carlut, Luis M Martinez, Felipe Criado-Boado, Johannes Müeller, Andy Clark
pmc-11461058.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). This article proposes a novel computational approach to embodied approaches in cognitive archaeology called computational cognitive archaeology (CCA). We argue that cognitive archaeology, understood as the study of the human mind based on archaeological findings such as artefacts and material remains excavated and interpreted in the present, can benefit from the integration of novel methods in computational neuroscience interested in modelling the way the brain, the body and the environment are coupled and parameterized to allow for adaptive behaviour.

pmc-13170905.title: Chronic tonsillitis and its potential alternative treatment: Exploration of the antibacterial activity of ethanolic Mentha piperita leaf extract against bacterial isolates from patients
pmc-13170905.creator: Puti G Munirwan, Lily Setiani, Benny Kurnia, Novina Rahmawati, Azwar Ridwan
pmc-13170905.description: Chronic tonsillitis is commonly associated with persistent bacterial infection, predominantly involving Gram-positive organisms, and increasing antimicrobial resistance has encouraged exploration of alternative therapeutic agents derived from medicinal plants. Mint leaves (Mentha piperita) are known to contain bioactive compounds with potential antibacterial activity; however, their antibacterial efficacy against isolates specifically obtained from patients with chronic tonsillitis has not been clearly established.

pmc-13178307.title: Correlation of pretreatment imaging features with lung shunt fraction in patients with large hepatocellular carcinoma (maximum diameter >8 cm) planned for 90Y-SIRT
pmc-13178307.creator: Lu Kuang, Xiaoxin Yang, Huanyu Gong, Jingjie Shang, Bin Guo, Qijun Cai, Yingxin Li, Le Bai, Jian Gong, Yong Cheng, Hao Xu
pmc-13178307.description: BackgroundYttrium-90 selective internal radiation therapy (90Y-SIRT) is an established therapy for unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), whose safety may depend on accurate lung shunt fraction (LSF) assessment. An elevated LSF may increase radiation pneumonitis risk and require dose modification. LSF quantification requires invasive technetium-99m macroaggregated albumin (99mTc-MAA) scintigraphy, while the effectiveness of noninvasive predictors has not been established.

pmc-13288613.title: Lost in translation: interferon-stimulated genes targeting flavivirus protein synthesis
pmc-13288613.creator: Marion Cannac, Jim Zoladek, Sébastien Nisole
pmc-13288613.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Flaviviruses are positive-sense RNA viruses that rely entirely on host translation machinery to express their genome, making protein synthesis a central point of vulnerability. Interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) exploit this dependence through diverse and mechanistically distinct strategies. PKR and IFIT proteins interfere primarily with translation initiation by targeting initiation factors or cap recognition, whereas SLFN11 and SAMD9L impair elongation through codon- and tRNA-dependent mechanisms. In parallel, ZAP, SHFL, and ISG20 inhibit translation by excluding viral RNAs from ribosomes or promoting their degradation.

pmc-13625227.title: Healthcare waste: from incineration to pyrolysis: a comparative life cycle assessment of two different healthcare plastic waste management processes
pmc-13625227.creator: Brett Duane, James Larkin, Marta Arias, Siri Stabel Olsen, Giulia Ligabue, Gabriele Donati, Gaetano Alfano, Daniel Eriksson, Diego Angelino, Evelien Fiselier, Stephanie DeSury, Ciaran Clissmann
pmc-13625227.description: BackgroundPlastic waste from healthcare is an increasing environmental challenge, particularly in resource-intensive clinical pathways such as dialysis. Peritoneal dialysis (PD) generates large quantities of single-use plastic materials, making its waste stream a priority for sustainable intervention. Conventional disposal through incineration contributes substantially to greenhouse gas emissions (GHG) and produces hazardous ash.
